capabilities: Edit 12 diagram kinds on a visual canvas
Format text from a customizable toolbar
Manage attachment folders and file names
disambiguation: Not a general Markdown syntax toolkit; its main job is visual editing of diagrams and tables that remain plain text.
extras: Five modules can be switched on or off individually; the file-explorer and attachment modules are off by default. No network requests, no account and no paid features; interface available in English and Simplified Chinese.
motivation: The author wanted diagrams and tables to stay as plain text in the note, with the editor as a visual layer over that text rather than a second copy of it.
problem: Diagrams in notes usually end up as screenshots or exported attachments, so they stop changing alongside the prose.

relations.evidence: Icon and interaction ideas come from the Obsidian core editor and editing-toolbar.

summary: Toolkit that visually edits diagrams, mind maps and formula tables inside fenced code blocks and writes changes back as plain text.
